title: Fluids at Rest and in Motion
subject: Physics

questions.question: The pressure at a point in a fluid at rest depends on
options: The depth below the surface and the density of the fluid
The surface area of the fluid
questions.explanation: The pressure at a point in a fluid at rest is given by P = ρgh, where ρ is the fluid density, g is acceleration due to gravity, and h is the depth below the surface. It depends on depth and density, not on the shape, volume, or surface area of the container.

questions.question: Pressure at a point in a fluid acts
questions.explanation: By Pascal's principle, pressure at a point in a fluid at rest is transmitted equally in all directions.

questions.question: At the same horizontal level in a continuous body of the same liquid at rest, the pressure is
questions.explanation: In a continuous body of the same liquid at rest, all points at the same horizontal level experience the same pressure.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of pressure is
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force / Area = N / m² = N m-2 (pascal, Pa).

questions.question: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid of density ρ is given by
questions.explanation: The pressure due to a liquid column at depth h is P = hρg (or ρgh).

questions.question: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 10m in water of density 1000kgm<sup>-3</sup>. [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
The atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately
questions.explanation: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 1.0 × 105 Pa (760 mmHg).

questions.question: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is the
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: The instrument used to measure the pressure of a gas in a laboratory is the
questions.explanation: A manometer measures the pressure of a gas in a laboratory.

questions.question: A barometer reads 760mmHg at sea level. If the atmospheric pressure is 1.0 × 10<sup>5</sup>Pa, the density of mercury is approximately
The pressure of a gas is 75cmHg. Express this in Nm<sup>-2</sup>. [density of mercury = 1.36 × 10<sup>4</sup>kgm<sup>-3</sup>, g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted
options: Equally in all directions throughout the fluid
Only to the walls of the container
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid.

questions.question: A hydraulic press has a small piston of area 0.01m<sup>2</sup> and a large piston of area 0.5m<sup>2</sup>. If a force of 20N is applied to the small piston, the force on the large piston is
questions.explanation: By Pascal's principle: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ ⇒ 20/0.01 = F₂/0.5 ⇒ F₂ = (20 × 0.5)/0.01 = 1000 N.

questions.question: In a hydraulic press, the force multiplication is achieved because
options: Pressure is greater on the larger piston
Pressure is the same on both pistons
The larger piston has less area
The small piston moves a greater distance
questions.explanation: In a hydraulic press, the pressure is the same on both pistons. Since F = P × A, a larger area gives a larger force.

questions.question: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid is equal to the
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: upthrust = weight of the fluid displaced by the body.

questions.question: A body displaces 0.2kg of water when fully immersed. The upthrust on the body is [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight of water displaced = mg = 0.2 × 10 = 2.0 N.

questions.question: A body weighs 50N in air and 30N when fully immersed in water. The upthrust on the body is
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight in air − weight in water = 50 − 30 = 20 N.

questions.question: A body weighs 60N in air and 40N when fully immersed in water. The relative density of the body is
questions.explanation: Upthrust = 60 − 40 = 20 N. Relative density = weight in air / upthrust = 60/20 = 3.

questions.question: A solid floats in a liquid when its
options: Weight is greater than the upthrust
Weight is equal to the upthrust
Density is greater than that of the liquid
Volume is greater than that of the liquid
questions.explanation: A floating body is in equilibrium when its weight equals the upthrust.

questions.question: A body of density ρ<sub>s</sub> floats in a liquid of density ρ<sub>l</sub>. The fraction of the body submerged is
questions.explanation: For a floating body, fraction submerged = density of body / density of liquid = ρs/ρl.

questions.question: A wooden block of density 0.6gcm<sup>-3</sup> floats in water. The fraction of its volume submerged is
questions.explanation: Fraction submerged = density of wood / density of water = 0.6/1.0 = 0.6.

questions.question: When a ship sails from fresh water to sea water, it
questions.explanation: Sea water is denser than fresh water, so the ship displaces less water for the same weight and therefore rises slightly.

questions.question: A hydrometer is used to measure the
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures the relative density of a liquid.

questions.question: The pressure at a depth of 5m in a liquid of density 800kgm<sup>-3</sup> is [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
The pressure in a liquid at a given depth is independent of the
questions.explanation: Pressure at a given depth depends on density, g, and depth, but not on the shape of the container.

questions.question: A U-tube contains water and oil. If the height of the water column is 10cm and that of the oil column is 12.5cm, the relative density of the oil is
questions.explanation: At the same level, pressures are equal: ρwaterghw = ρoilgho ⇒ ρoil/ρwater = hw/ho = 10/12.5 = 0.8.

questions.question: The equation of continuity for an incompressible fluid flowing through a pipe of varying cross-section is
questions.explanation: Equation of continuity: A1v1 = A2v2 (volume flow rate is constant).

questions.question: Water flows through a pipe of cross-sectional area 0.02m<sup>2</sup> at a speed of 2ms<sup>-1</sup>. The volume flow rate is
questions.explanation: Volume flow rate = A × v = 0.02 × 2 = 0.04 m3 s-1.

questions.question: If the cross-sectional area of a pipe is halved, the speed of the fluid flowing through it
questions.explanation: By continuity, A1v1 = A2v2. If A2 = A1/2, then v2 = 2v1. Speed doubles.

questions.question: Bernoulli's principle states that as the speed of a fluid increases, its
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle: as fluid speed increases, its pressure decreases (for horizontal flow).

questions.question: The Bernoulli's equation for fluid flow is given by
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation: P + ½ρv2 + ρgh = constant.

questions.question: Torricelli's theorem gives the speed of efflux from a small hole at depth h as
questions.explanation: Torricelli's theorem: v = √(2gh).

questions.question: Water flows out of a small hole at the bottom of a tank filled to a height of 5m. The speed of efflux is [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
The Venturi meter is used to measure the
options: Rate of flow of a fluid
questions.explanation: A Venturi meter measures the rate of flow of a fluid.

questions.question: An airplane wing is designed so that air flows faster over the top surface than the bottom. This creates
questions.explanation: Faster flow on top means lower pressure on top, so there is greater pressure on the bottom, providing lift.

questions.question: Viscosity is the internal friction between
options: Two layers of a fluid in relative motion
questions.explanation: Viscosity is the internal friction between two layers of a fluid in relative motion.

questions.question: As the temperature of a liquid increases, its viscosity
questions.explanation: As temperature increases, molecular kinetic energy increases, so viscosity decreases.

questions.question: Stokes' law gives the viscous drag F on a small sphere of radius r moving with velocity v in a fluid of viscosity η as
questions.explanation: Stokes' law: F = 6πηrv.

questions.question: A small ball falling through a viscous liquid attains terminal velocity when the
options: Net force on the ball is zero
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, the ball moves with constant velocity, so the net force is zero.

questions.question: The terminal velocity of a small sphere falling through a viscous liquid is directly proportional to
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity vt ∝ r2. So it is directly proportional to the square of the radius.

questions.question: Streamline flow is also known as
questions.explanation: Streamline flow is also called laminar flow.

questions.question: The Reynolds number is used to determine whether fluid flow is
questions.explanation: The Reynolds number determines whether flow is laminar or turbulent.

questions.question: The equation P + ½ρv<sup>2</sup> + ρgh = constant is valid for
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation is valid for ideal (non-viscous, incompressible) fluid flow.

questions.question: A fluid flows through a horizontal pipe. At a point where the pipe narrows, the speed of the fluid increases and the pressure
questions.explanation: By Bernoulli's principle, as speed increases, pressure decreases.

questions.question: The force on a dam due to water depends on
options: The depth of water and the area of the dam
The shape of the dam only
questions.explanation: The force on a dam depends on the depth of water and the area of the dam (pressure varies with depth).

questions.question: The pressure at the bottom of a container of liquid is independent of the
questions.explanation: Pressure at the bottom depends on depth, density, and g, but not on the shape of the container.

questions.question: A balloon filled with helium rises in air because
options: The upthrust of air is greater than the weight of the balloon
questions.explanation: Helium is lighter than air, so the upthrust (weight of air displaced) is greater than the weight of the balloon, causing it to rise. Both A and B are correct.

questions.question: The atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude because
options: The density of air increases with altitude
The weight of the air column above decreases
The wind speed increases with altitude
questions.explanation: As altitude increases, the weight of the air column above decreases, so atmospheric pressure decreases.

questions.question: The pressure of a gas in a closed container is due to
options: The weight of the gas molecules
Collisions of gas molecules with the walls of the container
The volume of the gas molecules
questions.explanation: Gas pressure is due to collisions of gas molecules with the walls of the container.

questions.question: A fluid is flowing through a pipe of non-uniform cross-section. If the speed at a point where the area is 0.1m<sup>2</sup> is 4ms<sup>-1</sup>, what is the speed where the area is 0.2m<sup>2</sup>?
questions.explanation: By continuity: A1v1 = A2v2 ⇒ 0.1 × 4 = 0.2 × v2 ⇒ v2 = 0.4/0.2 = 2 m/s.
